summary: No findings. CI: the new 'Playtest' step is a static literal command (no ${{ }} expressions, no github.event/head_ref interpolation, so no workflow command injection); no if:, continue-on-error, '|| true' or set +e, so a non-zero exit fails the job (guarded by tests/ci/workflow.test.ts). Workflow-level permissions remain 'contents: read', no secrets used, action pins unchanged. Violation output: the block is built only from engine/runner state of seeded bot hands (numbers, seat numbers, fixed words, formatCard text, describeAction text, and a replay code that is either computed by handReplayCode or already validated by isReplayCode as 32 lowercase hex). Size and button are range-checked integers. No raw argv, env or user data reaches the output. Seams: PlaytestSeams (makePolicy, onAction, engine) are only an optional third parameter of main/playHand/runPlaytest; tools/playtest/main.ts calls main(argv, io) with no seams and parseArgs adds no options, so CLI input cannot select a custom engine or hook. tests/support/faulty-engine.ts is not imported from src/ or tools/. No new dependencies; randomness unchanged (deterministic test seeds, not security-relevant). Resource use: checker work is O(state size) per action, and the summary retains only the first violating hand, so memory stays bounded; the --hands upper bound (1e9) is unchanged from TASK-1.6 and is a local-dev CLI only.
